chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer, from his father who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the salt wherein is saffron, for the one in Ihraam?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for the one in Ihraam that he should eat anything wherein is saffron, nor anything from the perfumes.'

key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in Ihraam (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihraam to eat salt mixed with saffron?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of perfume (*tayyib*) for the Muhrim extends to ingestion, not just topical application. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the sensory essence of the prohibited item, such as saffron, renders it impermissible to consume, thereby broadening the scope of *Ihram* restrictions beyond mere external use.
